title: Wingy Manone, Eddie Condon and the Chicago Blue Note
summary: Dance reads a string of 1946-49 jobs; Zutty was with Wingy Manone in California but joined Condon in Chicago, with Bobby Hackett, Bud Freeman and Peanuts Hucko at the Blue Note.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well this thing where you've got here Zutty. Galliard Slim '46. Wingy Manone (Wingy Lemone?) '47. Eddie Condon '48. Joe Marsala '48, Nappy Lamare '49. Were these sort of mostly things you were working out of California?
No. Condon (Norman?) was out on the road. He was with Wingy (Wingy?) in California.
Yes, I was with Wingy Manone (Wingy?) (Lemone?) out in California. But I joined Condon in Chicago.
See, because Condon had Bud Freeman, Peanuts Hucko and Dick Cary on piano and Dave Manning on bass.
Bobby Hackett, yes. Bobby Hackett and a fine trombone player was out of Fred Waring's band, he was on the trombone. And that's when we played at, that place on Randolph Street?
